Install and load necessary modules

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

```

Creating Vector

```{r}
# Create a vector of your target counties and states for easy filtering
US_border_counties <- data.frame(
  State_Name = c("California", "California",
                 "Arizona", "Arizona", "Arizona", "Arizona",
                 "New Mexico", "New Mexico", "New Mexico",
                 "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas",
                 "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas", "Texas"),
  County = c("San Diego County", "Imperial County",
             "Yuma County", "Pima County", "Santa Cruz County", "Cochise County",
             "Hidalgo County", "Luna County", "Doña Ana County",
             "El Paso County", "Hudspeth County", "Jeff Davis County",
             "Presidio County", "Brewster County", "Terrell County",
             "Val Verde County", "Kinney County", "Maverick County",
             "Webb County", "Zapata County", "Starr County", "Hidalgo County", "Cameron County")
)
```

Food Insecurity Variable

```{r}
# Read in data 

US_food_insecurity <- read_excel("MMG2025_2019-2023_Data_To_Share.xlsx", sheet = "County")

head(US_food_insecurity) # Check the data 

# Create US total data frame while averaging all the years together per county
US_total <- US_food_insecurity %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    US_Food_Insecurity_Rate = mean(`Overall Food Insecurity Rate`, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

US_total

# Separate the "County, State" column into two columns
US_food_insecurity <- US_food_insecurity %>%
  tidyr::separate(
    col = `County, State`,           # The column to separate
    into = c("County", "State_Name"), # New column names
    sep = ", ",                      # Separator to split on
    remove = TRUE                    # Remove the original column
  )

# Check the result
head(US_food_insecurity)

# Filter and calculate average food insecurity rates for border counties
US_border_county_data <- US_food_insecurity %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(US_border_counties, by = c("County", "State_Name")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(County, State_Name) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Avg_Food_Insecurity_Rate = mean(`Overall Food Insecurity Rate`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# View the result
print(US_border_county_data)

```

Poverty Rate Variable

```{r}


## US Total Poverty Rates 
# Read in the data 
US_poverty <- read_excel("Poverty Rate US past 5 years.xlsx", sheet = "Data")

head(US_poverty) # Check the data 

US_total <- US_total %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    US_Poverty_Rate = US_poverty[[3, 6]]
  )
US_total

## County Poverty Rates

# Read data
US_county_poverty <- read_excel("Poverty Rate per county past 5 years.xlsx", sheet = "Data")

# Get county column indices (every 5th column starting from the first county)
county_cols <- names(US_county_poverty)[stringr::str_detect(names(US_county_poverty), "County")]
county_indices <- which(names(US_county_poverty) %in% county_cols)

# Extract all data at once using vectorized operations
US_poverty_data <- data.frame(
  County = stringr::str_extract(county_cols, ".*?County") %>% stringr::str_trim(),
  State_Name = stringr::str_extract(county_cols, "(?<=,\\s).*") %>% stringr::str_trim(),
  Poverty_Rate = US_county_poverty[3, county_indices + 4] %>%
    unlist() %>%
    stringr::str_remove("%") %>%
    as.numeric() / 100
)

# Join with your existing data
US_border_county_data <- US_border_county_data %>%
  dplyr::left_join(US_poverty_data, by = c("County", "State_Name"))

US_border_county_data
```

Educational Attainment Variable 

```{r}

# Read in the data 

US_education <- read_excel("Educational Attainment US total past 5 years.S1501-2025-11-18T220033.xlsx", sheet = "Data")

head(US_education)

# Clean and extract the education rates
education_rates <- US_education %>%
  # Filter for rows containing education attainment data
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(...1, "High school graduate or higher|Bachelor's degree or higher")) %>%
  # Select the label and percentage columns
  dplyr::select(education_type = ...1, percent_estimate = ...4) %>%
  # Convert percentages to numeric (remove % and convert)
  dplyr::mutate(
    percent_numeric = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(percent_estimate, "%") ~ as.numeric(stringr::str_remove(percent_estimate, "%")),
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(percent_estimate) * 100  # Convert decimal to percentage
    )
  ) %>%
  # Group by education type and calculate average
  dplyr::group_by(education_type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(avg_rate = mean(percent_numeric, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Extract the specific values
avg_hs_rate <- education_rates %>%
  dplyr::filter(education_type == "High school graduate or higher") %>%
  dplyr::pull(avg_rate)

avg_bachelor_rate <- education_rates %>%
  dplyr::filter(education_type == "Bachelor's degree or higher") %>%
  dplyr::pull(avg_rate)

# Add to your existing US_total dataframe
US_total <- US_total %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    US_HS_Graduate_Rate = paste0(round(avg_hs_rate, 1), "%"),
    US_Bachelor_Rate = paste0(round(avg_bachelor_rate, 1), "%")
  )

# View the result
print(US_total)

## Read in County Education Data 
county_education <- read_excel("Educational Attainment per county last 5 years.xlsx", sheet = "Data")

county_education

# Function to extract percentages and calculate averages
process_education_data <- function(data) {
  # Get column names that contain county names (every 12th column starting from 2)
  county_cols <- seq(2, ncol(data), by = 12)
  county_names <- names(data)[county_cols]
  
  # Initialize results dataframe
  results <- data.frame(
    County = character(),
    Avg_HS_or_Higher = numeric(),
    Avg_Bachelors_or_Higher = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Process each county
  for(i in seq_along(county_cols)) {
    col_start <- county_cols[i]
    county_name <- county_names[i]
    
    # Extract percentage column (2 positions after county name column)
    pct_col <- col_start + 2
    
    if(pct_col <= ncol(data)) {
      # Get all percentage values from this county
      pct_values <- data[[pct_col]]
      
      # Find rows with "High school graduate or higher" and "Bachelor's degree or higher"
      hs_rows <- which(grepl("High school graduate or higher", data[[1]], ignore.case = TRUE))
      bach_rows <- which(grepl("Bachelor's degree or higher", data[[1]], ignore.case = TRUE))
      
      # Extract percentages for high school and bachelor's
      hs_pcts <- pct_values[hs_rows]
      bach_pcts <- pct_values[bach_rows]
      
      # Convert percentage strings to numeric (remove % and convert)
      hs_numeric <- as.numeric(gsub("%", "", hs_pcts)) / 100
      bach_numeric <- as.numeric(gsub("%", "", bach_pcts)) / 100
      
      # Remove NA values and calculate averages
      hs_avg <- mean(hs_numeric, na.rm = TRUE)
      bach_avg <- mean(bach_numeric, na.rm = TRUE)
      
      # Add to results
      results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
        County = county_name,
        Avg_HS_or_Higher = hs_avg,
        Avg_Bachelors_or_Higher = bach_avg
      ))
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# Process the education data
education_averages <- process_education_data(county_education)

# Extract state information BEFORE cleaning county names
education_averages <- education_averages %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Extract state from the original county string
    State_Name = stringr::str_extract(County, "(?<=, ).*$"),
    # Clean county name (remove state part)
    County = stringr::str_replace(County, ",.*", "") %>%
      stringr::str_trim()
  )

# Join with your border county data using BOTH County and State_Name
US_border_county_data <- US_border_county_data %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    education_averages %>% 
      dplyr::select(County, State_Name, Avg_HS_or_Higher, Avg_Bachelors_or_Higher), 
    by = c("County", "State_Name")
  )

# View the results
print(US_border_county_data)

```

Rent / Income Variable 

```{r}

library(readr)

## Read in Rent Data 

average_rent <- read_csv("RentData.csv")

head(average_rent)

# Check class of rent variable 
class(average_rent$B25058EST1)

## Create US Rent DF - Multiply by 12 to get annual rent 
US_Average_Rent <- average_rent %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    US_Average_Rent = mean(B25058EST1, na.rm = TRUE) * 12
  )

# Add the annual rent into the US_total df
US_total <- US_total %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    US_Rent = US_Average_Rent$US_Average_Rent
  )

# View result
print(US_total)

# Filter and calculate average rent rates for border counties
border_rents <- average_rent %>%              # average_rent is RentData.csv
  dplyr::mutate(
    State_join  = STATE_NAME,                 # "Arizona", "California", etc.
    County_join = paste0(NAME, " County")     # "Cochise County", "El Paso County", etc.
  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    border_counties,
    by = c("State_join" = "State_Name",
           "County_join" = "County")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(State_join, County_join) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Avg_Rent = mean(B25058EST1, na.rm = TRUE) * 12, # Multiply by 12 to turn monthly to yearly
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    State  = State_join,
    County = County_join
  )

# View the result
print(border_rents)


## Read in Income Data 

average_income <- read_csv("IncomeData.csv")

head(average_income)

# Check class of rent variable 
class(average_income$B19013EST1)

## Create US total data frame while averaging all the years together per county
US_Average_Income <- average_income %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    US_Average_Income = mean(B19013EST1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

US_Average_Income # Check average 

## Add to existing US Total DF

US_total <- US_total %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    US_Income = US_Average_Income$US_Average_Income
  )

## Calculate Annual Rent / Income for US Total 
US_total <- US_total %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    US_Rent_to_Income_Pct = US_Rent / US_Income
  )



# Filter and calculate average rent rates for border counties
border_incomes <- average_income %>%              # average_rent is RentData.csv
  dplyr::mutate(
    State_join  = STATE_NAME,                 # "Arizona", "California", etc.
    County_join = paste0(NAME, " County")     # "Cochise County", "El Paso County", etc.
  ) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    border_counties,
    by = c("State_join" = "State_Name",
           "County_join" = "County")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(State_join, County_join) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Avg_Income = mean(B19013EST1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    State  = State_join,
    County = County_join
  )

# View the result
print(border_incomes)


# Join rent and income data for border counties
border_rent_income <- border_rents %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    border_incomes,       # <— replace with your actual income df name if different
    by = c("State", "County")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Rent_to_Income_Pct = Avg_Rent / Avg_Income
  )

print(border_rent_income)

# Join with your existing data
US_border_county_data <- US_border_county_data %>%
  left_join(border_rent_income, 
            by = c("County" = "County", 
                   "State_Name" = "State"))

US_border_county_data

```

Food Access Variable 

```{r}


food_access <- read_excel("FoodAccessResearchAtlasData2019.xlsx", sheet = "Food Access Research Atlas")

head(food_access)

# Check class and fix to numeric 
class(food_access$lapop1share)


food_access$lapop1share <- parse_number(food_access$lapop1share)


## Create US total data frame while averaging all the years together per county
US_total_food_access <- food_access %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    US_Food_Access_Rate = mean(lapop1share, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

US_total_food_access

## Add to Total US DF

US_total <- US_total %>%
  mutate(
    US_Food_Access_Rate = US_total_food_access$US_Food_Access_Rate
  )

# Filter and calculate average food access rates for border counties
border_food_access <- food_access %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    border_counties,
    by = c("County" = "County", "State" = "State_Name")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(State, County) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Food_Access_Rate = mean(lapop1share, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# View the result
print(border_food_access)


# Add to the final data frame 
US_border_county_data <- US_border_county_data %>%
  left_join(border_food_access, 
            by = c("County" = "County", 
                   "State_Name" = "State"))

US_border_county_data
```
